exposure: Time interval between EA administration and chorioamnionitis/fever onset (<6, 6-12, >12 h)
outcome: Adverse neonatal outcomes (e.g., transient tachypnea of the newborn)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1,933 women diagnosed with chorioamnionitis who underwent a term vaginal delivery attempt at a university affiliated medical center between 2003 and 2015.
finding: Neonatal and maternal outcomes are similar in febrile laboring women regardless of epidural analgesia (EA) administration, and the time interval between EA and onset of fever is not associated with increased rates of neonatal fever or adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Higher rates of instrumental deliveries were observed in the epidural analgesia group compared to the non-EA group.
